big_idea: TELL TIME in hours, minutes, seconds. Use the right TOOL for each measurement.
learning_intention: We are learning to tell time and pick the right measurement tool.
student_learning_goal: I can tell time and pick the right measurement tool.
success_criteria: I can READ analog and digital clocks.
I can MEASURE perimeter and area.
I can MEASURE capacity and mass.
I can PICK the right tool for the job.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Cal: TIME on analog and digital clocks. Today's BIG case — perimeter, area, capacity/mass, and TIME! Roo + Cal open: 'Measure AROUND, measure the FILL, measure the TIME!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets in farmer hats. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. Last 4 days we did perimeter, area, area in cm², capacity and mass. Today we add TIME!'

Define time. 'TIME on clocks: HOURS, MINUTES, SECONDS. Two clock types: ANALOG (hands) and DIGITAL (numbers).'

Demo analog. 'Hour hand short, minute hand long. 3:45 — hour at 3, minute at 9.'

Demo digital. '3:45 PM = same time, just numbers.'

Seconds. 'Second hand sweeps around. 60 sec = 1 min. 60 min = 1 hr.'

'Cal says — both clocks tell the SAME time, different style.'

Now show 4 clock cards:
- Analog 9:00 / Digital 9:00
- Analog 3:30 / Digital 3:30
- Analog 12:15 / Digital 12:15
- Analog 6:45 / Digital 6:45

Class reads each.

Now show the 4 capstone stations:
- Station 1: PERIMETER — measure 2 polygons.
- Station 2: AREA — count cm² for 2 shapes.
- Station 3: CAPACITY/MASS — compare 2 cards.
- Station 4: TIME — read 4 clocks.

Each child rotates 6 min per station and records on TEMPLATE.

'Roo and Cal say — pick the RIGHT TOOL for each job!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 4 stations rotation (~6 min each).
Stretch: write a 'farmer's brag' — one sentence per station.
Help with clock reading at Station 4.
STRATEGY COMPARE at perimeter station: pause at minute 15. Two children share strategies. Class debates which is more efficient. Cite Earnest (2017) on time + space integration.
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'Same job, two paths. Pick the one that fits the shape.'

differentiation.for_extending: Write digital and analog for each clock.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 4 stations physically. NO-MATERIALS PATH: replace stations with body math — perimeter = pace around a square; area = sit in rows × columns; capacity = how many children fit in the carpet circle; time = body-clock pose for hour/minute.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: perimeter; area; capacity/mass; time.

consolidation.activity_name: Roo and Cal's Big Farm Brag
consolidation.exit_routine: Roo + Cal capstone refrain — Roo: 'Measure AROUND, measure the FILL!' Cal: 'Measure the TIME!' Class: 'That's MEASUREMENT!' (3x). Each child shares one station's tool + reading.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child reads ANALOG hands wrong — repairing the hour/minute mix-up trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the time-and-farm capstone, the trap is hour/minute confusion: child reads 3:45 as '3 hours and 45 hours' or '3 minutes and 45 hours' (Friedman & Laycock 1989; Earnest 2017 on children's clock reading). Without time fluency, the capstone integration fails.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: perimeter (L1), area (L2), cm² (L3), capacity/mass (L4) plus introducing TIME at 5-min intervals.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Time station. Clock shows 3:45 (hour at 3, minute at 9). Child reads '9:15'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Cal asks — which hand is SHORTER?'

Probe. 'Short hand = HOUR. Long hand = MINUTE. Hour hand is at 3, so 3:something. Minute hand at 9 → 9 × 5 = 45 minutes. So 3:45.'

Generalise. 'Cal says — short = hour, long = minute. ALWAYS!'

If still mixed: cover one hand at a time. 'Just the SHORT hand — what hour? Now just the LONG hand — what minute?'
common_misconceptions: Both hands point at 9. (Repair: read each separately.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child says hours instead of minutes: drill 'minute hand POINTS to minutes; hour hand POINTS to hours'; physical clock demo.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child reads 5-min increments: drill 5, 10, 15, 20...60 by 5s while pointing at clock positions.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child tells time but stuck on elapsed: drill 'count from start time IN 5-MIN HOPS to end time.'
